subject: Support package options for ACME platform - tranche pricing and SLA uplift
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Dow <emily.dow@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Support package options for ACME platform - tranche pricing and SLA uplift

Hi Emily / ACME procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great discussion on the latency and failover patterns you see during peak data ingests. Per our conversation, I put together a short set of support packaging options that map to the operational risks you described. Attached: redwood_support_pricing_v1.pdf (summary) + follow-up worksheets.

High level:
- Base: 99.9% uptime SLA, support during business hours, incident response SLA of 4 hours, standard operational reporting.
- Uplift: 99.95% SLA, 24/7 triage channel, on-call escalation within 60 minutes, prioritized engineering escalation queue.
- Premium: 99.99% SLA, assigned escalation manager, quarterly architecture reviews, and a guaranteed 30-minute triage window for sev1.

I also sketched a tranche/pricing approach where discounts improve as you commit to higher annual spend tiers (helps keep unit economics predictable for both sides). The PDF has ballpark numbers, but I wanted to validate your priorities before we pick numbers: is the priority minimizing worst-case downtime (favoring Premium) or predictable monthly unit cost (favoring Base + credits)?

Next steps proposed:
1) Quick call (30m) to confirm which environment(s) need uplift (prod only vs prod+canary).
2) If uplift desired, we can propose a tranche discount schedule and an implementation credit to offset onboarding.

If helpful I can include our security/compliance pack and a sample implementation credit addendum.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachment: redwood_support_pricing_v1.pdf (6 pages, pricing summary)

From: Emily Dow <emily.dow@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support package options for ACME platform - tranche pricing and SLA uplift

Jonas — thanks for the clear options. A few clarifying questions before we take this to procurement: 

1) For the uplift vs premium tiers, what are the concrete credits if we miss the SLA? Our procurement team will want the credit ladder (e.g., 99.95 -> X% credits).
2) Does the tranche discount require the entire commit up front, or can it be annualized monthly with a financial commitment?
3) We run a cross-region canary in eu-west and want to understand regional failover guarantees and whether that counts toward the uptime calculation.
4) Is an implementation credit (to help offset migration engineering) a one-time credit or amortized over the first 12 months?

We have an internal preference to anchor around 99.95 with a modest uplift to 99.99 if we see capacity/demand growth — but cost is a factor. Can you capture a couple of concrete pricing points and the credit ladder and we can share with procurement for an initial read?

Thanks — looping procurement to track.
Emily
Emily Dow
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Systems
emily.dow@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ACME tranche/credit asks — internal pricing posture

Internal — quick note before Jonas replies to ACME:

We can structure this as a 3-tranche commitment: $300k/yr, $600k/yr, $1.2M/yr. Proposed discounts: 5% / 10% / 16% off list for support pricing if the commit is annualized (we can accept monthly billing with an annual commitment signature).

Concessions we can offer without exec approval:
- One-time implementation credit up to $25k for the 1.2M tier (covers one week of migration support).
- Regional failover: count cross-region canary only toward SLA if active health checks are proxied through the primary region (we'll need config).

Exec-only concession to accelerate: additional 4% price uplift (i.e., total 20% max) or extend the implementation credit to $40k. Markus — can you confirm if we can approve the extra 4% at your discretion for strategic logos?

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Dow <emily.dow@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support package options for ACME platform - tranche pricing and SLA uplift

Emily — thanks, answers inline and an updated offer below. Attached: tranche_pricing_breakdown.xlsx and implementation_credit_terms.docx.

1) Credit ladder (example):
- If monthly uptime < 99.9%: 10% service credit of monthly support fee
- If monthly uptime >= 99.9% and < 99.95%: 5% credit
- If monthly uptime >= 99.95% and < 99.99%: 2% credit
- If monthly uptime < 99.99% (i.e., below premium target): escalate to account owner + remediation plan; large outages evaluated case-by-case.

2) Tranche billing: We support annualized commitment with monthly invoicing. Commitment signature required; discount levels apply pro rata to consumption over the year (true-up at year end).

3) Regional failover: By default SLA is measured per-tenant across primary regions. We can include eu-west canary in the SLA calculation if your canary traffic is routed through the same HA health checks — this is an engineering config, not a pricing blocker.

4) Implementation credit: one-time credit applied as invoice offset in month 1; for the 1.2M tranche we propose $25k (we can discuss amortization but our legal prefers one-time offsets).

Proposed example pricing (support fee only, illustrative):
- Tier A (no commit): $12,500/mo, 99.9% SLA, business-hours support, 4h triage.
- Tier B (commit $600k/yr): $8,900/mo (approx 10% discount), 99.95% SLA, 24/7 triage, 60m escalation. Includes 12 hours of onboarding support and KB integrations.
- Tier C (commit $1.2M/yr): $7,500/mo (approx 16% discount), 99.99% SLA option available as add-on + assigned escalation manager. Includes $25k implementation credit.

If these align, can we schedule a 30m procurement call Monday to confirm the commitment cadence and sign instrument?

Next steps I propose:
- Procurement call (30m) — confirm contract cadence and signatory.
- If ACME wants the exec-only concession (extra 4%), mention and we'll loop Markus for approval.

Thanks — I can update the term sheet and send a redline-friendly DocuSign link after we confirm.

Jonas
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachment: tranche_pricing_breakdown.xlsx (detailed tiers)

From: Emily Dow <emily.dow@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support package options for ACME platform - tranche pricing and SLA uplift

Jonas / Vanessa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the concrete numbers. Procurement is good to move forward with an annualized commitment model; we will aim for the $1.2M tranche if we can get the $25k implementation credit and the confirmation on the 99.99% add-on availability.

Two asks before we lock: 
1) Can you confirm the exact wording for the SLA credit ladder in the contract (procurement prefers explicit percentages and triggers).
2) Please send the DocuSign and we'll get this to our CFO for sign-off; target is to have an executed agreement by end of month.

If you can loop Markus if the extra 4% concession is required, we may ask for it during CFO review.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Systems
emily.dow@acme.com
